issues.legal_issue: Land-rights modifications made through consolidation and village-planning measures that form part of an agrarian-reform scheme are protected against constitutional property-rights challenges when they serve the planned use and welfare of the rural community.
material_facts: During consolidation proceedings, land held by proprietors was reserved for village panchayats and community purposes, including schools, roads, health facilities, manure pits, and other village needs.
Some land was reserved for non-proprietors, including for housing and village services; the affected proprietors received no compensation.

The challenged measures operated together with legislation on consolidation, village panchayats, common lands, and security of land tenure, as part of a wider programme of land redistribution and rural planning.
The proprietors challenged the measures and legislation as unconstitutional for modifying or taking their property without compensation.
issues.conclusion: The challenged modifications formed part of a general scheme of agrarian reform and were protected by Article 31-A; the challenge based on Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 therefore failed, and the appeals were dismissed. The court distinguished Kochuni because it concerned a bare transfer of rights without a change in tenure or an agrarian-reform purpose.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31-A, including its provisions concerning acquisition or modification of rights in an estate, is construed broadly to protect legislation forming part of agrarian reform. Such reform can include measures ancillary to land redistribution that plan rural areas and promote the productive use of land and community welfare. The court relied on Atma Ram v. State of Punjab; Gangadhar Narayanrao Majumdar v. State of Bombay; Ram Narain Medhi v. State of Bombay; Sonapur Tea Co. Ltd. v. Must. Mazirunnessa; Burrakur Coal Co. Ltd. v. Union of India; State of Bihar v. Rameshwar Pratap Narain Singh; State of Bihar v. Umesh Jha; and the distinction from K. K. Kochuni v. State of Madras. It upheld the High Court’s approach in Jagat Singh v. Punjab State. Relevant provisions included Article 31-A, Articles 19(1)(f) and 31, sections 18, 2(bb) and 23-A of the East Punjab Holdings (Consolidation and Prevention of Fragmentation) Act, section 19 of the Punjab Gram Panchayat Act, and sections 3, 4, 6 and 7 of the Punjab Village Common Lands (Regulation) Act.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_land_realloc: People challenge the constitutionality of measures that reallocate or modify rights in land.
predicates.land_taken_from_proprietors_without_comp: A public authority takes, reserves, or reallocates land held by proprietors without paying them compensation.
predicates.land_reserved_for_village_community_uses: Land is reserved for management by a village body or for facilities and uses that benefit the village community.
predicates.land_allotted_to_nonproprietors: Land is allotted to people who did not previously hold proprietary rights in it.
predicates.measures_form_part_of_integrated_rural_r: The land measures form part of a broader programme of land reform and rural planning, rather than a bare transfer of property rights.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns uncompensated land reallocation that serves village-community needs or non-proprietors and forms part of integrated rural reform, the land-rights modifications are protected from constitutional property challenges.
